images.title: Folding a straight angle
images.purpose: Folding a straight angle so the two arms overlap gives a crease that cuts it into two equal angles.
images.composition: One straight line across the middle with one ray standing up from the centre, lots of space above and below.
images.exact_structure: One horizontal straight line AB in grey #6B7280 with the point O at its exact middle. One ray OC rising straight up from O at exactly 90 degrees. The left angle AOC is shaded teal #0072B2 and the right angle COB is shaded amber #E69F00, exactly equal in size, each with a small arc. Exactly 4 labelled points, 2 shaded angles.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
any of the following: a crease that is not exactly in the middle
images.takeaway: The crease splits a straight angle into two equal angles.
images.description: A horizontal line AB with O in the middle and a vertical ray OC; the left angle teal and the right angle amber are equal.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at the two angles and say how they are alike.

image_decisions.why: The fold-in-half idea for a straight angle is one picture of two equal angles on a line.
